## Learning Objective

Use and interpret the "~" symbol in the context of random variables.


## Lesson

When we're talking about random variables,
the "~" symbol can be read as "is distributed as".
For example, $X\sim N(0,1)$
means that $X$ is a normal random variable with expected value (mean) 0 and variance 1.
The mean and variance are the parameters of the normal distribution.

Similarly, $X\sim\text{Poisson}(\mu)$ means that $X$ is a Poisson random
variable with mean $\mu$.
The mean is the only parameter of the Poisson distribution.

## Problems

### Problem 1

How do you interpret $X\sim\text{Bernoulli}(p)$?

::: {.callout-tip title="Solution" collapse="true"}

$X$ is a Bernoulli random variable with parameter $p$.
You may not have learned this yet,
but $p = P(X = 1)$.
The important thing is just to recognize what $\sim$ means
and to recognize that $p$ is a parameter.

:::
